'''Michel Spiro''' (born 24 February 1946 in [[Roanne]], [[Loire (department)|Loire]], France) is a French [[physicist]] and was President of the [[List of presidents of the CERN Council|CERN Council]] between 2010 and 2013.

== Biography ==
Michel Spiro attended [[Secondary education in France|the high school]] Jean-Puy de Roanne. Spiro obtained the [[baccalauréat]] in 1963, with a specialisation in [[elementary mathematics]]. After this, he attended the school
[[Lycée Louis-le-Grand]]  to prepare his entry exam at the [[École polytechnique (France)|École polytechnique]]. He completed his graduate studies in [[theoretical physics]] in 1969. 
 
He joined the [[French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission]] (CEA) in 1970, as an engineer. He was promoted to the position of director of the Particle Physics Section of the Department of Astrophysics, Particle Physics, Nuclear Physics and Associated Instrumentation (DAPNIA ) in 1991 and led the section until 1999. He became chargé de mission of the CEA and assistant scientific director in [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique]] (CNRS), responsible for astroparticle physics and neutrinos. He took over the leadership of DAPNIA in 2002. From 2003 to 2010 he was appointed director of [[Institut national de physique nucléaire et de physique des particules]] (IN2P3) in CNRS.<ref name="bioInter">{{cite web |url=https://attract-eu.com/profile/michel-spiro/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191003175338/https://attract-eu.com/profile/michel-spiro/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=3 October 2019 |title=Michel Spiro, Emeritus Research Director, CEA |date=3 Oct 2019 |website=ATTRACT }}</ref>

Spiro obtained his PhD <ref>{{cite thesis |type=PhD |last=Spiro |first=Michel |date=1977 |title=Etude des résonances mésoniques étranges produites dans les interactions K<sup>−</sup>p à 14,3 GeV/c |publisher=CEA|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/118213/}}</ref> from [[University of Paris-Sud]], [[Orsay]] in 1976. His early research in particle physics led him, as a member of the [[UA1 experiment]], to participate in the discovery of the intermediate [[W and Z bosons|bosons W and Z]].<ref From 1983 to 1999, Professor Spiro lectured [[quantum mechanics]], then [[stellar equilibrium]] and [[stellar evolution|evolution]] and finally energy and environment at the [[École Polytechnique]].<ref name=PCCP />

From 2010 to 2013 he was President of [[List of presidents of the CERN Council|CERN Council]]. His presidency overlapped with the start of [[Large Hadron Collider|LHC]] physics.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=Agnieszka Zalewska elected president of CERN council |url=https://home.cern/news/news/cern/agnieszka-zalewska-elected-president-cern-council|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190613161521/https://home.cern/news/news/cern/agnieszka-zalewska-elected-president-cern-council|url-status=dead|archive-date=13 June 2019|work=CERN News |location=Geneva |date=20 September 2012 |access-date=13 June 2019 }}</ref> Since then Spiro helds the position as research director emeritus at the [[French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission|CEA]].

Michel Spiro was president of the [[French Physical Society]] from 2016 to 2017<ref>{{cite news|language=fr|title=Michel Spiro - Le CERN, le LHC et la découverte du Boson de Higgs|journal=[[France Culture]]|date=2013-06-22 |url=http://www.franceculture.fr/conferences/universite-de-nantes/michel-spiro-le-cern-le-lhc-et-la-decouverte-du-boson-de-higgs|access-date=2018-05-22}}</ref> and president-elect for [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]] (IUPAP) as of 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Executive Council: Officers 2017-2020 {{!}} IUPAP: The International Union of Pure and Applied Physics|url=http://iupap.org/executive%2Dcouncil%2Dand%2Dcommission%2Dchairs/executive%2Dcouncil%2Dofficers%2D2017%2D2020/|website=iupap.org|language=en|access-date=2019-04-02|archive-date=2019-04-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190402222305/http://iupap.org/executive-council-and-commission-chairs/executive-council-officers-2017-2020/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In October 2019 Spiro was asked to replace IUPAP president [[Kennedy J. Reed]] who wanted to step down for personal reasons.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://iupap.org/news2/presidents-resignation-new-leadership/|title=Presidents' resignation – new leadership|website=IUPAP|access-date=25 November 2019|archive-date=29 November 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191129134053/http://iupap.org/news2/presidents-resignation-new-leadership/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |last=McKellar |first=Bruce |author-link=Bruce McKellar |date=December 2019 |title=New leadership of IUPAP |url=http://iupap.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/12/IUPAP_dec2019_low.pdf |magazine=IUPAP Newsletter |access-date=5 December 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=Spiro appointed IUPAP president |url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/2701615 |journal=CERN Courier |volume=59 |issue=6 |pages=54 |access-date= 5 December 2019 }}</ref> As of 2025 Spiro continues as IUPAP past president under the presidency of [[Silvina Ponce Dawson]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=iupap |date=2024-10-28 |title=Silvina Ponce Dawson IUPAP new President - IUPAP: The International Union of Pure and Applied Physics |url=https://iupap.org/2024/10/28/silvina-ponce-dawson-iupap-new-president/ |access-date=2025-01-20 |language=en-US}}</ref>

From June 2020 to December 2025, Michel Spiro was chair of the [[CERN & Society Foundation|CERN and Society Foundation]] Board,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Michel Spiro and Fido Dittus take the leadership of the CERN & Society Foundation|url=https://home.cern/news/news/cern/michel-spiro-and-fido-dittus-take-leadership-cern-society-foundation|access-date=2020-09-17|website=CERN|language=en}}</ref> a foundation to support and promote the mission of CERN, the [[European Organization for Nuclear Research]], and disseminate its benefits to the wider public. In March 2024, he was appointed chair of the Curie and Joliot-Curie Association, succeeding to [[Édouard Brézin|Edouard Brezin]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Organisation et statuts |url=https://curie-joliotcurie.fr/qui-sommes-nous/organisation-et-statuts/ |access-date=2024-12-19 |website=Association Curie et Joliot-Curie |language=fr-FR}}</ref>

Spiro chaired during 2022 and 2023 the steering committee of the [[International Year of Basic Sciences for Sustainable Development]] (IYBSSD2022). He also contributed towards the proclamation on August 25, 2023, by the United Nations General Assembly, of an International Decade of Sciences for Sustainable Development 2024 to 2033.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://documents-dds-ny.un.org/doc/UNDOC/GEN/N23/256/93/PDF/N2325693.pdf?OpenElement |title=Resolution adopted by the General Assembly on 25 August 2023: International Decade of Sciences for Sustainable Development, 2024–2033 |publisher=United Nations |year=2023 |edition=A/RES/77/326 |location=New York}}</ref> In this framework he chairs [[The Earth-Humanity Coalition]] during the year 2024.
